blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Consensus, caution and the British long view are sometimes caricatured as slowness or indecision. They are neither. At their best, they are a deliberate approach to running institutions built to last — companies meant to outlive their founders, partnerships that span generations, reputations treated as inheritances from colleagues who came before and loans from those who will come after.

Consensus, in this spirit, is not a committee decision. It is the habit of making sure the people whose support you will need next year, not just this quarter, feel that their concerns were weighed. Caution is not timidity. It is the discipline of asking, before any major move, what the world will look like if this goes wrong — and whether the organisation could survive that version of itself. The long view is not slowness. It is the willingness to trade a shiny quarter for a steady decade.

These three habits, practised consistently, produce the kind of leader British institutions have always admired: unshowy, unhurried, and very hard to replace. The leaders who learn to be patient in the right way end up holding almost every conversation that matters — for a very long time.

items.q: How does the author characterise consensus, caution and the long view?
options: As unavoidable weaknesses of large organisations
As a deliberate approach to running lasting institutions
As tactics reserved for moments of crisis
As synonyms for slowness and indecision
items.why: "They are a deliberate approach to running institutions built to last."

items.q: According to the text, what does consensus in this spirit actually require?
options: That every objection be resolved before acting
That those whose future support you need feel their concerns were weighed
A committee empowered to make the final decision
A unanimous vote from every stakeholder
items.why: "the people whose support you will need next year… feel that their concerns were weighed" — alinhamento, não unanimidade.

items.q: What is caution said to be, in the author's definition?
options: A preference for delegating hard decisions
A reluctance to take any risk
The discipline of testing whether the organisation could survive if a move goes wrong
A way of slowing rivals down
items.why: "the discipline of asking… whether the organisation could survive that version of itself."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Trading a strong quarter for a strong decade can be wise.
A patient leader can become very hard to replace.
Caution and consensus are essentially symptoms of indecision.
Reputations should be treated as inheritances and loans.
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre justamente refutando a ideia de que essas virtudes são indecisão.

items.q: The phrase "trade a shiny quarter for a steady decade" suggests that the author values…
options: durable, long-term results over short-term shine
items.why: Inferência: a metáfora contrapõe o brilho passageiro do trimestre à solidez de uma década.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James encerrar o programa de liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, as we close, let me leave you with the three people I keep coming back to. None of them were the loudest voice in any room I shared with them. That is rather the point.

The first taught me that consensus is not about winning the meeting. It is about making sure the person who disagrees with you today will still take your call in three years. She lost more arguments than anyone I knew, and she outlasted every one of us.

The second was almost maddeningly cautious. Before any acquisition he would ask one question — what does this look like if it fails, and can we live with that morning? Half the deals he walked away from later collapsed for someone else. We only noticed years afterwards.

And the third simply refused to be hurried. He would say the market rewards the impatient once and punishes them repeatedly. He was unshowy, almost invisible, and quite impossible to replace.

If you take one thing from this week, take this: patience, practised deliberately, is not a personality trait you were either born with or not. It is a discipline. Learn it, and you will still be in the conversations that matter long after the hurried have moved on.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did the three leaders James describes have in common?
options: They all left the organisation early
None of them was the loudest voice in the room
They preferred to make decisions alone
They were the most senior people in the firm
items.why: "None of them were the loudest voice in any room… That is rather the point."

items.q: According to James, what did the first leader believe consensus was really about?
options: Ensuring the person who disagrees today still takes your call in three years
items.why: "consensus is not about winning the meeting… the person who disagrees with you today will still take your call in three years."

items.q: What can we infer from "Half the deals he walked away from later collapsed for someone else"?
options: The deals failed because of his involvement
His caution repeatedly proved to be sound judgement
The cautious leader was afraid of all decisions
items.why: Inferência: o fato de os negócios ruírem para outros mostra que a cautela dele era acerto, não medo.

items.q: What does the third leader mean by "the market rewards the impatient once and punishes them repeatedly"?
options: The market never rewards bold moves
A single early win rarely offsets the later, recurring costs of haste
Patient investors are punished by the market
Impatience always pays off in the long run
items.why: Inferência: o ganho pontual da pressa é superado pelas perdas que se repetem depois.

items.q: What is James's central message about patience in his closing?
options: It is only useful for junior managers
It matters less than speed in modern markets
It is an inborn personality trait you either have or lack
It is a deliberate discipline that can be learned
items.why: "patience, practised deliberately, is not a personality trait… It is a discipline. Learn it."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Their approach was often caricatured as mere hesitation." To be caricatured is to be…
options: portrayed in a distorted, oversimplified way
items.why: Caricatured = caricaturado: retratado de forma distorcida e simplificada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "His refusal to rush was mistaken for weakness, when in fact it was a ___ strategy."
items.why: Deliberate = deliberado, intencional — o oposto de fraqueza casual.

items.q: "She treated the firm's reputation as an inheritance, not an asset to spend." An inheritance here is…
options: something valuable passed down to be preserved
items.why: Inheritance = herança: algo de valor recebido para ser preservado e transmitido.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Caution, in his view, was never ___ — it was the courage to imagine failure before acting."
items.why: Timidity = timidez; o texto contrapõe cautela a timidez.

items.q: "The most admired leaders were unshowy and hard to replace." Unshowy means…
items.why: Unshowy = discreto, sem ostentação; o oposto de autopromoção.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs de negócios ligados ao tema. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "He would never sign off on a deal he could not live with if it failed." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "The board agreed the vision but never followed through on it." They…
options: failed to see it through to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto.

items.q: "A single flashy quarter will not move the needle on a decade-long reputation." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; com "not", nega esse efeito.

items.q: "Several partners pushed back on the aggressive timeline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Rather than force the issue, she chose to hold off on the announcement until the team was aligned." To hold off on means to…
items.why: Hold off on = adiar de propósito, esperar o momento certo.
